headlines.title: Western Union Yields Nearly 15%. These 3 High-Yield Stocks Haven’t Raised Their Dividends in Years
headlines.summary: When a dividend refuses to budge for years, the payout may be hiding a problem. Three big-yield stocks have frozen their checks, and one already swung the axe. Which warning signs separate a patient income stock from a trap?

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz (KHC) Climbed, But What Is Drawing Fresh Attention?
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz (KHC) has kicked off a five year global partnership with the NFL, tying core brands like Velveeta and Kraft Mac & Cheese to marquee football events. Recent trading has been supportive for Kraft Heinz, with a 1-month share price return of 7.2% and an 8.7% share price gain year to date. The 1-year total shareholder return of 10.6% contrasts with a 3-year total shareholder return that is down 10.

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz (KHC) Stock Looks Fairly Valued On Its Sales Base
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz has shifted its listing to the New York Stock Exchange and the share price has climbed in the short term, which puts a fresh spotlight on whether the current valuation is supported by the company’s sales base. With investors hearing an updated growth story through 2029, the key issue is how much of that outlook is already embedded in the US$26.51 share price. Over the past 3 years the stock has declined 10.

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
headlines.summary: The company, halfway through year one of a five-year deal with the league, has already seen signs that its quirky activations are driving results.

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz vs. On: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
headlines.summary: Kraft Heinz trades at a lower forward multiple, while On's revenue is growing at a far faster clip, so the right pick depends on how much risk you're willing to carry.

description: The Kraft Heinz Company, together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and markets food and beverage products in North America and internationally. Its products include condiments, sauces, dressings, and spreads; cheese, frozen potato products, and other frozen meals; meal kits, frozen snacks, and pickles; dry packaged desserts, refrigerated ready to eat desserts, and other dessert toppings; ready to drink and powdered beverages, and liquid concentrates; American sliced and recipe cheeses; mainstream coffee, coffee pods, and premium coffee; and cold cuts, bacon, and hot dogs. It offers its products under the Kraft, Oscar Mayer, Heinz, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Ore-Ida, Capri Sun, Maxwell House, Kool-Aid, Jell-O, ABC, Master, Quero, Golden Circle, Wattie's, Pudliszki, and Plasmon brands, as well as Bagel Bites, Claussen, A1, and Cool Whip. It sells its products through its own sales organizations, as well as through independent brokers, agents, and distributors to chain, wholesale, cooperative, and independent grocery accounts; convenience, value, and club stores; pharmacies and drug stores; mass merchants; foodservice distributors; institutions, including hotels, restaurants, bakeries, hospitals, health care facilities, and government agencies; and various e-commerce platforms and retailers. The company has a strategic partnership with the National Football League. The company was formerly known as H.J. Heinz Holding Corporation and changed its name to The Kraft Heinz Company in July 2015. The company was founded in 1869 and is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
